records.title: A use for this
records.prose: I had been rubbing every tree in the meadow. This flat thing reaches the part they miss. Kept my back under it until the itch went quiet. Nobody can have it. I found what it is for.
records.identityEvidence: Adult male; sex explicit in avatar source. Other selected adults are visually compatible but not sexed by their records.
records.visibleScene: A bison presses its upper back beneath an interpretive sign; another bison is partly visible behind it.
records.fictionBoundary: The sign contact is visible. Prior unsuccessful rubbing, relief and ownership are fiction. Human artifact appropriation is the proposed mechanism; lead should reject if too close to Crispin scratching.
records.creator: NPS/Neal Herbert

records.title: Feet above everything
records.prose: Put all four feet in the air. The ground took the rest of me without complaint. Rocked once. Twice. Got a whole shoulder rubbed before I remembered I had been showing the other bull how large I was.
records.identityEvidence: Adult male; sex explicit in avatar source. Other selected adults are visually compatible but not sexed by their records.
records.visibleScene: A bison rolls onto its back in a dusty wallow, with a rear hoof raised.
records.fictionBoundary: Rolling is visible. The earlier display and lapse of attention are fiction; no second bull is claimed visible. The turn is display interrupted by pleasure, not another dust application.
records.creator: NPS/Jim Peaco

records.title: The strip between us
records.prose: Dug my head down to the grass. He swept his snow into my hole. I swept it back. There is quite a strip of bare ground between us now. Neither of us is eating.
records.identityEvidence: Adult male; sex explicit in avatar source. Other selected adults are visually compatible but not sexed by their records.
records.visibleScene: Two bison lower their heads into snow beside exposed ground beneath snowy mountains.
records.fictionBoundary: Snow feeding is supported by the source. Reciprocal sweeping, ownership of a hole and suspended eating are fictional temporal actions.
records.creator: NPS/Neal Herbert

records.title: Learning its reach
records.prose: I took the soft edge in my teeth and leaned back. It came with me a little. I pulled harder. When I let go, it slapped my chin. Bit it again, very close to where it lay.
records.identityEvidence: Adult female in fiction. Avatar source gives species but no sex or precise age; adult-sized appearance is compatible, not female identification.
records.visibleScene: An American badger plants its front claws on an old tire lying in dry grass.
records.fictionBoundary: The tire and contact are visible. Biting, stretching a worn edge and the resulting recoil are invented. The tire never rolls or springs upright.

records.title: Two quick learners
records.prose: My daughter bit her brother. I put my mouth over her back and held her still. She went limp. Her brother took the opportunity to bite her. Had to put her down to reach him.
records.holdReason: Hold for image quality: the maternal group supports the central relationship, but the 1176 by 963 original is soft and grainy. Prose retained for candid review, not admission.
records.identityEvidence: Adult female in fiction. Avatar source gives species but no sex or precise age; adult-sized appearance is compatible, not female identification.

records.fictionBoundary: Mother and two young are explicit. Kit sexes, reciprocal bites and intervention are fiction. Do not assert a visible scruff grip.

records.title: Near enough
records.prose: My mother licked my head. I licked the leg nearest me. She moved it, so I followed. She moved it again. We got halfway around each other before she lay down and let me reach her face.
records.identityEvidence: Male, from calf memory to adult. Avatar and antlered adults are male; calf sex unrecorded.
records.visibleScene: An elk cow licks the forehead of a small calf in green woodland.
records.fictionBoundary: Maternal licking is visible. The calf is unsexed in the record; fictional Cedric is male. Reciprocal licking, circling and lying down are imagined. The central event is returning affection across a size difference.
records.creator: NPS / Chalice Keith

records.title: Into the branches
records.prose: All summer I took the long way around branches. Today I drove my antlers straight into one. The loose velvet caught and pulled away. I stopped with my head bent, waiting for the hurt. There was only the branch tugging. Pushed farther in.
records.identityEvidence: Male, from calf memory to adult. Avatar and antlered adults are male; calf sex unrecorded.
records.visibleScene: Loose strips of velvet hang from a bull elk antler; recently exposed antler surfaces appear beneath them.
records.fictionBoundary: Shedding is explicit. Branch contact, anticipation and the individual sensation are fiction. This is not a general claim that all velvet shedding is painless.
records.creator: NPS

records.title: Last year's gap
records.prose: I knew where to put my head. We fought last autumn. Slid into the old gap and met a new tine. We are standing very carefully while I learn this year's version of him.
records.identityEvidence: Male, from calf memory to adult. Avatar and antlered adults are male; calf sex unrecorded.

records.title: Across the old antler
records.prose: Found last year's antler in the grass. Put my forehead against it out of habit. Nothing happened. Stepped over it. Came back and stepped over it again.
records.identityEvidence: Male, from calf memory to adult. Avatar and antlered adults are male; calf sex unrecorded.
